title: PQFA: Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation of Fused Representations for Multimodal Classification
abstract: Most multimodal learning methods improve how heterogeneous representations are aligned and fused, while post-fusion enhancement remains less explored. We propose Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation (PQFA), a hybrid quantum-classical framework that applies multiple shallow variational quantum circuits to fused multimodal features. Text and image representations extracted by frozen RoBERTa and ViT encoders are processed through bidirectional cross-attention, attentive pooling, and adaptive gated fusion. The fused feature is then amplitude-encoded into parallel quantum circuits, whose measurement readouts are concatenated with the classical representation for prediction. We evaluate PQFA on MM-IMDb and N24News through controlled comparisons using the same encoders, fusion backbone, data splits, projection dimension, and augmentation output width. PQFA consistently outperforms both the fusion backbone without quantum augmentation and a width-matched MLP augmentation baseline, while using approximately 2.2K augmentation parameters compared with 24.0K for the MLP branch. Missing-modality experiments further show improved robustness when textual or visual inputs are incomplete, with particularly clear gains when the more informative textual modality is severely degraded. Controlled ablations and feature-space analyses indicate that the improvement cannot be reproduced by random feature mappings, increased classical width, or untrained quantum transformations. Quantum-state diagnostics additionally show stable predictive performance across the tested simulated noise levels and distinct branch-specific transformations of the encoded states. These results establish PQFA as an effective and parameter-efficient strategy for post-fusion augmentation in hybrid quantum-classical multimodal learning.
summary: The paper introduces Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation (PQFA), a novel hybrid framework that enhances multimodal feature representations by passing the fused classical output through parallel shallow quantum circuits. By demonstrating superior performance and parameter efficiency compared to purely classical augmentation techniques, PQFA establishes quantum readout as an effective tool for post-fusion learning in complex AI tasks.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is enhancing multimodal classification by improving representations *after* they have been fused, rather than redesigning the entire fusion backbone.
main_result: PQFA consistently outperforms both unaugmented baselines and MLP augmentation methods on benchmark datasets while using significantly fewer parameters, demonstrating effective post-fusion quantum feature augmentation.
method: The method involves amplitude-encoding the classical fused feature into multiple parallel shallow variational quantum circuits (PQCs) whose measurement readouts are concatenated with the original classical representation for final prediction.
model_or_system: It employs a hybrid quantum-classical framework. Classical components use frozen RoBERTa and ViT encoders followed by cross-attention, pooling, and adaptive gated fusion to yield $\mathbf{z}_C$. This is then augmented by parallel PQCs acting on the fused feature.
key_observables: Classification accuracy improvement over baselines; stable predictive performance across simulated noise levels; parameter efficiency compared to classical alternatives.
important_parameters: The number of augmentation parameters (PQFA uses $\approx 2.2\text{K}$ vs. $24.0\text{K}$ for MLP-Aug); the depth and width of the variational quantum circuits.
main_assumptions: The performance gains are attributed to the learned nonlinear transformation provided by the quantum readouts, not merely increased feature dimensionality or trainable parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture: Text/Image $\rightarrow$ Encoders $\rightarrow$ Cross-Attention $\rightarrow$ Pooling $\rightarrow$ Adaptive Gating ($\mathbf{z}_C$) $\rightarrow$ Parallel Quantum Augmentation (PQCs) $\rightarrow$ Concatenation $\rightarrow$ Classifier.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for post-fusion enhancement. It details the PQFA architecture, which processes fused features through parallel quantum circuits. Evaluation involves controlled comparisons against unaugmented and MLP baselines, followed by ablation studies (missing modalities, feature diagnostics) to prove the necessity of the quantum component.
why_interesting: This work directly applies variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) in a hybrid setting for complex data classification, offering a structured way to test quantum advantage in machine learning tasks beyond simple kernel methods or state preparation.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overall architecture of the proposed Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation (PQFA) framework. Text and image inputs are first encoded by frozen pretrained Transformer encoders. The extracted unimodal token features are projected into a shared latent space, refined by bidirectional cross-attention, summarized by attentive pooling, and fused through an adaptive gating module. The fused classical representation is then processed by two paths: a direct classical path and a parallel quantum augmentation path based on amplitude encoding and multiple shallow parameterized quantum circuits. Figure 2: Schematic illustration of the Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation module. (a) A shallow brickwall parameterized quantum circuit used in each quantum branch. (b) The predefined brick pool consisting of multiple local two-qubit parameterized blocks, which introduces structural diversity across parallel quantum branches.

Figure 3: Fine-grained comparison between PQFA and MLP-Aug on MM-IMDb. (a) Per-label F1 difference across genres sorted by support. (b) Mean sample-wise Jaccard gain grouped by MLP-Aug prediction uncertainty. Positive values indicate that PQFA outperforms the width-matched classical augmentation baseline.

Figure 4: PCA cumulative explained variance of augmentation features on MM-IMDb. Faster saturation indicates stronger variance concentration in fewer principal directions, whereas slower saturation indicates a more dispersed augmentation feature space.

Figure 5: Post-training noisy inference analysis on MM-IMDb. Panel (a) reports Micro-F1 under different noise probabilities, and panel (b) reports the quantum readout drift Dq. All model parameters are fixed during this analysis.
